2439: Among the textural parameters, hardness correlated with gumminess (r = 0.913) and chewiness (r = 0.816), as is to be expected since both are computed from hardness (Bourne, 2002). Springiness correlated with amylose (r = 0.640) and cohesiveness with amylose (r = 0.484), which supports the contention that the elastic recovery of the steamed product is contingent upon the amylose network formed on cooling (Tester et al., 2004). Resistant starch was negatively correlated with the predicted glycaemic index (r = -0.587), in accordance with Frei et al. (2003) and Sajilata et al. (2006). Ash correlated with calcium (r = 0.804), indicating that the mineral load of the product was governed principally by the calcium contributed by the fortifying material.
2440: Overall acceptability was negatively correlated with total carbohydrate (r = -0.895), non-resistant starch (r = -0.716), starch (r = -0.710), springiness (r = -0.691) and lightness (r = -0.662), and positively correlated with total flavonoid (r = 0.782), total antioxidant activity (r = 0.780), total phenol (r = 0.773), hue angle (r = 0.762), phytate (r = 0.753) and total soluble protein (r = 0.746). The panel therefore favoured the darker, less starchy, softer and more antioxidant-rich products, which is precisely the profile of the fortified treatments. Aroma was the sole sensory attribute uncorrelated with overall acceptability (r = -0.123). Aroma and general palatability were thus governed by different constituents, and a high aroma score alone did not confer a high acceptability score.
2441: Taste, flavour, texture, appearance, cooking quality and overall acceptability were correlated with one another at unity in the present data, the six scores differing only by a constant. Their relations with the physico-chemical parameters are therefore identical, and only overall acceptability has been carried forward into the multivariate analysis that follows.
2449: Principal component analysis was performed on the standardised values of the forty two parameters over the twenty four treatment means. The purpose was to reduce the dimensionality of the data and to establish which parameters contribute most to the variation among the treatment combinations (Jolliffe, 2002; Granato et al., 2018). The eigenvalues and variance explained by the first eight components are given in Table 4.142, the scree plot in Fig. 4.99, the loadings in Table 4.143 and the biplot of the first two components in Fig. 4.100.
2450: Seven components returned eigenvalues exceeding unity and were retained following Kaiser (1960). The first component alone explained 50.12% of the total variation and the second 14.12%, the two together therefore explaining 64.24%, while the first five explained 86.66%. A first component of this magnitude indicates that a single principal gradient accounts for most of the variation among the twelve treatments.
2451: The loadings in Table 4.143 identify this gradient unambiguously. The positive pole of the first component was defined by total antioxidant activity (1.005), total phenol (0.968), total flavonoid (0.942), total soluble sugar (0.905) and overall acceptability (0.874); the negative pole by total carbohydrate (-0.988), non-resistant starch (-0.965), starch (-0.963), lightness (-0.927), yellowness (-0.893), chroma (-0.888), springiness (-0.875) and amylose (-0.836). The first component therefore separates the starchy, pale and firm plain products from the pigmented, antioxidant-rich, soft and well-liked fortified products, and may accordingly be designated a fortification axis.
2452: The second component was defined at its positive pole by total protein (0.922), aroma (0.658), manganese (0.617), gumminess (0.608) and hardness (0.592), and at its negative pole by resistant starch (-0.783), β-carotene (-0.644) and total colour difference (-0.590). This component separates the carrot-fortified treatments, rich in β-carotene and resistant starch, from the plain and beet-fortified treatments, which were higher in protein, aroma and firmness, and may accordingly be designated a carrot fortification axis.
2453: The biplot in Fig. 4.100 corroborates these findings. The twelve treatments separated into three groups along the first component in the order plain, carrot-fortified and beet-fortified, and within each group the four varieties followed the order Dudeshwar, Gobindabhog, Radhunipagal and Kalojira. KBI occupied the extreme positive position, proximate to the vectors of total phenol, total flavonoid, total antioxidant activity and anthocyanin, while DI occupied the extreme negative position, proximate to the vectors of total carbohydrate, starch and lightness. The two years of each treatment invariably fell close together, which demonstrates graphically that the treatment effects were stable across years and that pooling was valid (Granato et al., 2018).
2457: Components with an eigenvalue above unity were retained following the Kaiser criterion.
2463: Loadings above 0.70 in absolute value were treated as important contributors to the component concerned.
2466: Kaviyaselvan et al. (2026) prepared idli from pigmented rice cultivars of Tamil Nadu blended with pearl millet flour and determined colour, texture and nutritional characters to differ significantly among the products, the insoluble-bound phenolics constituting the dominant fraction and principal component analysis identifying the most promising formulations. The same approach, applied here to aromatic landraces and vegetable fortification, indicates beetroot-fortified Kalojira idli.
2468: Cluster analysis was performed on the standardised values of the forty two parameters of the twelve treatment combinations in order to group the treatments by overall quality. The squared Euclidean distance served as the measure of dissimilarity, and the groups were formed by the minimum variance method of Ward (1963), which is widely employed for food quality data on account of the compact, nearly equal groups it yields (Everitt et al., 2011). The dendrogram is given in Fig. 4.101, the composition of the clusters in Table 4.144 and the cluster means in Table 4.145.
2469: The cophenetic correlation coefficient was 0.793, indicating that the dendrogram represents the original distance matrix reasonably faithfully (Murtagh and Legendre, 2014). The twelve treatments resolved into four clusters at a linkage distance of approximately 9.4. Cluster I comprised the three plain products of the aromatic landraces, namely GI, KI and RI; Cluster II comprised DI alone; Cluster III comprised all four carrot-fortified products and Cluster IV all four beet-fortified products.
2470: The salient feature of this grouping is that the first division was determined by fortification and not by variety. All four beet-fortified treatments grouped together irrespective of parent variety, and the same obtained for the carrot-fortified treatments. This confirms the result of the principal component analysis, namely that the type of fortification constitutes the principal source of variation in product quality. Variety was operative only at the second level, where the plain product of the non-aromatic control separated from the plain products of the three aromatic landraces and formed a cluster of its own. This separation of DI is itself informative, since it indicates that the quality of the non-aromatic control differs from that of the aromatic landraces to a greater extent than any two aromatic landraces differ from each other.
2471: The cluster means in Table 4.145 characterise the four groups. Cluster IV, the beet-fortified group, returned the highest total phenol (265.22 mg GAE 100 g⁻¹), total flavonoid (142.75 mg QE 100 g⁻¹), total antioxidant activity (393.44 mg TE 100 g⁻¹), total soluble protein (2.24%), calcium (500.89 ppm), anthocyanin (1.41) and overall acceptability (8.06), together with the lowest amylose, starch, total carbohydrate and lightness. Cluster III, the carrot-fortified group, was intermediate for the bioactive fractions but returned by far the highest β-carotene (38.85), the highest resistant starch among the fortified groups (1.69%), the lowest predicted glycaemic index (60.49) and the highest redness (11.57). Cluster I, the plain aromatic group, returned high starch, high total protein (13.09%), the greatest hardness (114.11) and a moderate acceptability of 7.28. Cluster II, comprising DI alone, returned the highest amylose, starch and total carbohydrate and the lowest total phenol, flavonoid, antioxidant activity and overall acceptability (6.14).
2472: The clustering thus corroborates the results of the analysis of variance and the principal component analysis. Cluster IV is the group of choice where a functional product of high antioxidant value and high acceptability is required, and Cluster III where a provitamin A-rich product of low glycaemic response is required.
2476: Clustering was based on the squared Euclidean distance of the standardised values of the forty two parameters. The cophenetic correlation coefficient was 0.793.
2482: Cluster means were computed from the pooled treatment means of the two years.
2484: The results demonstrate that variety, type of fortification and their interaction all exerted a significant effect on the quality of idli prepared from aromatic rice. Fortification proved the stronger of the two factors, and both the principal component analysis and the cluster analysis identified it, rather than variety, as the principal source of variation.
2485: The three aromatic landraces were superior to the non-aromatic control Dudeshwar for protein, phenol, flavonoid, antioxidant potential and every sensory attribute. Among them, Kalojira was richest in the bioactive fractions, Gobindabhog richest in minerals with the lowest phytate, and Radhunipagal yielded the softest product. Beet extract elevated phenol, flavonoid, antioxidant activity, calcium and anthocyanin, while carrot extract supplied β-carotene and yielded the highest resistant starch with the lowest glycaemic index. Both softened the product and improved its colour and acceptability, and the sensory gain was uniform across all four varieties.
2486: KBI is therefore recommended as the superior combination, having returned the highest total phenol, flavonoid, antioxidant activity, soluble protein, anthocyanin and overall acceptability. KCI is indicated where a provitamin A-rich product of low glycaemic response is required, and GBI where a mineral-enriched product is required. The study demonstrates that the aromatic landraces of West Bengal may be converted into an attractive and nutritionally improved fermented food using carrot and beet extract alone, without recourse to any synthetic colour or additive.
